question_text: If 1, ω, ω² are the cube roots of unity, show that (1 − ω + ω²)⁶ + (1 + ω − ω²)⁶ = 128.

mark_split.label: Reduce each bracket to a multiple of ω

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this — what each bracket reduces to, and how the sixth powers are evaluated.
insider_note: Both brackets need the doubling: 1 + ω² = −ω gives −2ω, and 1 + ω = −ω² gives −2ω². The sixth power removes the minus sign and ω⁶ = ω¹² = 1, so each term is 64.

steps.label: Reduce each bracket to a multiple of ω
steps.margin_note: First mark. 1 + ω + ω² = 0 gives 1 + ω² = −ω and 1 + ω = −ω². So 1 − ω + ω² = −2ω and 1 + ω − ω² = −2ω²; each bracket has two equal terms, not one.

recall.must_convey: That 1 + ω + ω² = 0 and ω³ = 1 are used to reduce 1 − ω + ω² to −2ω and 1 + ω − ω² to −2ω².

the sum of the three cube roots is zero, so substitute

steps.why: Every ω question is the same two facts: ω³ = 1 (so high powers of ω reduce) and 1 + ω + ω² = 0 (so any two of 1, ω, ω² can be replaced by minus the third). The reduction is the mark; the arithmetic after it is short.
common_mistakes: Writing 1 − ω + ω² = 0 by mis-reading the sign in 1 + ω + ω² = 0.
Reducing to −ω instead of −2ω (forgetting the second −ω).
Expanding the sixth power by the binomial theorem.

steps.label: Evaluate the sixth powers
steps.margin_note: Second mark. (−2ω)⁶ + (−2ω²)⁶ = 64ω⁶ + 64ω¹² = 64(ω³)² + 64(ω³)⁴ = 64 + 64 = 128. An even power removes the minus sign.

recall.must_convey: That the reduced expression is evaluated to 128.
accept: evaluate the reduced form and get 128
simplify the powers of omega and the value is 128

steps.why: An even power removes the minus sign, 2⁶ = 64, and ω⁶ and ω¹² are powers of ω³ = 1. Everything reduces to numbers.
